## Ruling recorded — 2, as a director-seat class-one adjudication: the filter-builder dropdown speaks the protocol's operator set; camelCase is the deprecated alias accepted on read and rewritten on write; no spec card is filed for the ids the protocol does not name (director seat, decision batch #129 item 2, 2026-09-13)

Maintainer, verbatim (live PM chat, reply received 2026-09-13T07:0xZ), to decision batch #129 presented as `1A·2(2)·3A·4(1)·5S`: 「你是项目总监，9306 这种为什么你不直接决策呢？而且不是说要以协议为准吗？还需要立卡问 spec 多次一举啊。这个也需要更新skills。其他同意。」

The correction is taken as written, twice over. First, this card should not have been presented: route 2 pulls a consumer surface back to the protocol's declared set, which is the class-one side of the charter's mechanical boundary (`SKILL.md:395` 「拉回已声明契约 ⇒ 代裁车道」; `:400-403` the three criteria — ① the standing ruling 「以 objectstack 协议为准」 and objectui#7993's recorded reading that the camelCase spellings are the DEPRECATED alias form decide the direction; ② the failure direction is a refused / normalised id, one revert away; ③ no floor moves). Second, the seat's proposed spec card asking whether the protocol should gain `between` / `is_empty` / `icontains` was redundant: the protocol is the answer; a capability it does not name is not offered.

### What is ruled
1. `defaultOperators` in `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` emits the `FilterOperatorSchema` ids (`equals`, `not_equals`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equal`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equal`, `in`, `not_in`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`) and nothing else. The mirror type follows.
2. Stored filters carrying camelCase ids keep loading: `normalizeFilterOperator` accepts the camelCase spellings as deprecated aliases (objectui#7993) and the builder writes the canonical id back — a lossless read-side conversion, ⛔ not a second vocabulary.
3. The eight dropdown ids with no protocol twin: `before` / `after` → `less_than` / `greater_than` and `exists` / `notExists` → `is_not_null` / `is_null` (same semantics, folded on read); `between`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`, `containsCaseInsensitive` are removed from the dropdown — zero measured pull, and objectui#7379's semantic boundary forbids folding a case-insensitive contains onto `contains`. ⛔ No spec card. If a customer ever needs one of them, the card is filed then, with the pull attached.
4. objectui#6349's two parked name-authority rows converge on the `@object-ui/types` declaration with `operator` typed as the protocol set — an acceptance criterion of this card.
5. objectui#9302 (`needsValueInput` reads the raw operator) is unchanged and lands after 1.

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:ui` kept; `priority:p3` added (the user-visible symptom is already fixed by PR objectui#9305; this is contract alignment). Recorded for the maintainer's 追认表 as a class-one adjudication.

## Ruling amended — item 3 of 5651809976 was wrong: the protocol ALREADY names every capability the dropdown offers; nothing is removed, and objectui's own 14-member `FilterOperatorSchema` is the stale mirror (director seat, 2026-09-13T07:03Z)

Maintainer, verbatim (live PM chat, 2026-09-13T07:0xZ), minutes after the ruling above: 「协议就是答案，但是协议是否正确也是需要你考虑的，从平台长远合理性的角度考虑，并参考主流相关平台」

Acting on that, the seat read the protocol instead of the card's copy of it. `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:243` `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` is **20** members, ⛔ not 14:

```
equals not_equals contains not_contains icontains starts_with ends_with
greater_than less_than greater_than_or_equal less_than_or_equal in not_in
is_empty is_not_empty is_null is_not_null before after between
```

The 14-member `FilterOperatorSchema` this card quotes lives in objectui's `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts` — it is objectui's mirror, six members behind the protocol. ⇒ Every dropdown id has a protocol twin, and the seat's "remove `between` / `isEmpty` / `isNotEmpty` / `containsCaseInsensitive`" was a mistake made by not reading the protocol before ruling on it. Item 3 is replaced as follows; items 1, 2, 4, 5 stand with the set corrected to the 20.

### Corrected mapping (22 dropdown ids → protocol)
`equals`→`equals` · `notEquals`→`not_equals` · `contains`→`contains` · `containsCaseInsensitive`→`icontains` · `notContains`→`not_contains` · `isEmpty`→`is_empty` · `isNotEmpty`→`is_not_empty` · `greaterThan`→`greater_than` · `lessThan`→`less_than` · `greaterOrEqual`→`greater_than_or_equal` · `lessOrEqual`→`less_than_or_equal` · `before`→`before` · `after`→`after` · `between`→`between` · `in`→`in` · `notIn`→`not_in` · `startsWith`→`starts_with` · `endsWith`→`ends_with` · `isNull`→`is_null` · `isNotNull`→`is_not_null` · `exists`→`is_not_null` · `notExists`→`is_null` (the last two are the only ids with no twin of their own; they fold to the null checks). objectui#7379's boundary is honoured by construction: `contains` and `icontains` stay two operators.

### The protocol-correctness check the maintainer asked for
Judged against mainstream filter UIs (director-seat memory pointers, ⛔ not measured): Airtable and Notion offer *is empty / is not empty* and a case-insensitive *contains* as the default; Dataverse FetchXML has `between`, `begins-with`, `ends-with`, `null` / `not-null`, `in`; Salesforce list-view filters have equals / not equal / contains / starts with / less or greater than. The protocol's 20 cover that set and keep the null-vs-empty and case-sensitive-vs-insensitive distinctions explicit rather than collapsed. ⇒ The protocol is right as it stands; nothing to add, nothing to remove.

### Execution (replaces item 1 and 3)
1. `@object-ui/types`' `FilterOperatorSchema` becomes the protocol's set — import `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` from `@objectstack/spec/ui` rather than a local literal, so the mirror cannot fall behind again (the same reasoning the protocol's own docblock at `:257-268` gives for `isMultiOperator`).
2. `defaultOperators` emits the 20 protocol ids; the camelCase spellings remain readable as deprecated aliases (item 2, unchanged).

`pm:queue` / `domain:ui` / `priority:p3` unchanged.
